Subject: Model fit & tool-calling evals \u0014 next steps (Avery Analytics)

Hi Samira / Liam —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about the customer support routing and claims automation use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: evaluate model fit for intent extraction + structured output for the claims intake flow, including tool/function calls to your downstream case-creation API.
- Success criteria (agreed): >=95% JSON schema compliance for the structured output (fields: intent, entities[], confidence) on the 1k holdout set; end-to-end case creation success >=98% when function-calls are retried per policy.
- Immediate asks from us: your sample prompt set and a small proof-of-concept dataset (no PHI) to run our eval harness.

Recommended Redwood configs (initial):
- Model candidates: redwood/fast-13B-v2-8k (low-latency baseline), redwood/accurate-70B-32k-quantized (higher-quality baseline for corner cases).
- Inference profile: prefix-KV caching enabled, batch size tuned to sub-100ms p95 for single-turn extractions; structured-output parser enforced.
- Function-calling: we recommend using our JSON-schema enforcement hook + retries (retry on 429/5xx up to 2 times with exponential backoff).

I've attached a prompt set (avery_prompt_set_v1.json) and a short PDF with our benchmark harness and initial runbook (redwood_eval_benchmark_20270418.pdf). Link to the full benchmark + eval notebook is below.

Proposed next steps:
1) You upload a 200\u2013500 sample set (anonymized) \u2014 due Thu 22 Apr.
2) We run initial model-fit evals and return a short readout + failing examples by Mon 26 Apr.
3) Joint sync (30 min) to decide on pilot: model selection + rollout plan.

If that looks good I can loop in Solutions Eng to start the eval.

Thanks \u2014 talk soon.

\u2014
Marissa Cole

Samira \u2014

Perfect, thanks. We'll start the eval as soon as we get the sample. Quick answers to your questions: 

- JSON-schema enforcement: yes \u2014 Redwood's structured-output validator is schema-driven and can map or drop extra fields based on a configurable mapping. For onboarding I'd recommend we keep an allowlist of fields and a small transform script (we can share a starter mapping).

- Retry pattern: we recommend an exponential backoff starting at 200ms, multiplying by 2, with max 2 retries for 429/5xx. So: initial call, wait ~200ms on first failure (429/5xx), retry; on second failure wait ~400ms then final attempt. We also provide a dead-letter hook to surface items that never complete.

- Model recommendations: run the 13B-v2 as the baseline (fast), and the quantized 70B for edge cases. We'll capture token/timing profiles and JSON compliance rates for both. If you want, we can also run a lightweight ensemble pass focusing on confidence calibration.

I've uploaded a starter mapping and a short eval config to the Drive link (see related_links).

Next: Rishi/Sean \u2014 can you pick this up once Samira uploads the sample? Priority: schema compliance check + function-call retry implementation in the sandbox.

Thanks,
Marissa
